_method: ● = the lesson's Exit Ticket assesses the TEKS; ○ = students use it in the Concept Development or Problem Set but the Exit Ticket does not assess it; blank = the topic lists it but the lesson does not address it. Fluency Practice is not counted.

M2.L1.why: Exit Ticket: compare and subtract times (17 − 14 seconds). Time intervals are in seconds, which the TE notes go beyond the Grade 3 standard (minutes), so 3.7C is ○.

M2.L2.why: Exit Ticket: draw start/end times, find minutes elapsed (1:34 to 1:56). Students count on the number line rather than compute, so 3.4A is ○.

M2.L3.why: Exit Ticket: 19 min + 17 min word problem on a number line with an equation.

M2.S3-1.why: Exit Ticket: 23 min + 54 min, answer in minutes and in hours and minutes, show finish time on a clock.

M2.L4.why: Exit Ticket: 10 equal bags make 1 kg, so each is 100 g (base-ten relationship). Students build a kilogram with a pan balance and relate kg/g to the place value chart in the Problem Set.

M2.L5.why: Exit Ticket: read weights on scales and choose grams or kilograms. Weighing classroom objects in the Problem Set.

M2.L6.why: Exit Ticket: how much heavier (subtraction), weight of 4 backpacks and how many backpacks equal the suitcase (multiplication/division). Students weigh with spring scales in the lesson.

M2.L7.why: Exit Ticket: how many 100 mL scoops fill 1 L and how many 10 mL groups are in 1 L. Students predict and measure container capacity in the Problem Set.

M2.L8.why: Exit Ticket: read capacities on a vertical number line, find the difference between two containers.

M2.L9.why: Exit Ticket: total capacity of 3 cups, half of a cup, 3 cups of tea. The Problem Set mixes weight and liquid volume problems.

M2.L10.why: Exit Ticket: label place value units, write standard form, bundle 11 thousands into a ten thousand.

M2.L11.why: Exit Ticket: write numbers in expanded notation from expanded form and word form. Students label place value units.

M2.L12.why: Exit Ticket: order four 5-digit prices, build a 5-digit number to make a comparison true. Problem Set uses the place value chart.

M2.L13.why: Exit Ticket: read a golf ball's weight on a scale and round it to the nearest 10 g on the number line, explaining the halfway point.

M2.L14.why: Exit Ticket: round 26 and 276 to the nearest ten on a number line, explain an error rounding 603.

M2.L15.why: Exit Ticket: round 137, 1,761 and 685 to the nearest hundred on a vertical number line.

M2.L16.why: Exit Ticket: round to the nearest thousand and ten thousand on a number line.

M2.L17.why: Exit Ticket: add measurements with mental math or the algorithm, two-step jogging-minutes problem. Composing a larger unit in the algorithm.

M2.L18.why: Exit Ticket: add measurements composing twice, lemonade word problem.

M2.L19.why: Exit Ticket: estimate total practice minutes by rounding to the nearest 10 and 100 and explain.

M2.L20.why: Exit Ticket: subtract measurements decomposing once, two-step banner problem.

M2.L21.why: Exit Ticket: subtract measurements decomposing twice (700 − 592), sheep/cow weight problem.

M2.L22.why: Exit Ticket: estimate a missing weight by rounding two ways, find the actual weight, judge reasonableness.

M2.L23.why: Exit Ticket: estimate then find a total and a difference of milliliters.
